subject: Daz
fact: Daz filed away the observation that the two Drow had decided they weren't worth the effort.
source_quote: The two of them hadn't lowered their weapons so much as they'd decided we weren't worth the effort. I filed that away.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz appreciated that Nym used the past tense when referring to his concern for his safety.
source_quote: I appreciated the past tense. It did a lot of work.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed that the fact someone hired professionals rather than acting directly was the most interesting part of the situation.
source_quote: That last part was the interesting part.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz had been running a list in the back of his head since Velkynvelve of entities that wanted him dead.
source_quote: I'd been running a list in the back of my head since Velkynvelve — the kind of list you keep when your life depends on knowing who wants what.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized that until this moment, the list of entities wanting him alive and protected had been empty.
source_quote: Entities with motive to see me alive and sufficiently protected to require hired blades from Menzoberranzan — that list had, until approximately this moment, been empty.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed that asking the obvious question was important because the answer was rarely the obvious answer.
source_quote: You always ask the obvious question, because the answer is rarely the obvious answer.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz privately found Nym's elegant indifference toward Asha reassuring.
source_quote: Nym dismissed it with a kind of elegant indifference that I found, privately, somewhat reassuring.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed that a third 'bravo' is never sincere.
source_quote: Three *bravos*. I have found, as a general principle, that a third *bravo* is never sincere.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz thought that Kaelira’s puzzlement was genuine and not theatrical.
source_quote: And then she looked at me, and there was genuine puzzlement in it — not contempt, not theater. Actual, professional confusion at an anomaly that didn't fit the pattern she'd been given.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz considered himself a nobody — with no house, no lineage, no claim to Drow societal currency.
source_quote: I had no house. No lineage with the right names. No claim on any of the structures that give a Drow life its currency in Menzoberranzan.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed that someone in Menzoberranzan had paid a lot to keep him alive, and that the anonymity implied the payer had something to hide.
source_quote: In Menzoberranzan, that level of insulation around a financial transaction means exactly one thing: the payer has significant reason not to be associated with the purchase.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz privately thought that the entire chain of events might have started because someone decided to be friends with the wrong drow.
source_quote: The thought had a particular shape. Elegant, in the way that retrospective clarity sometimes is. The whole of it — the capture, the escape, Velkynvelve, the months of running — threading back to a single point. Me. A nobody. A nobody that someone in Menzoberranzan had interrupted their schedule over, more than once.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt he was standing at the edge of the question that changes everything, as described by Milo Goodbarrel.
source_quote: Milo Goodbarrel, that relentlessly hopeful halfling whose book I'd read too many times to admit, had a phrase for the sensation I was experiencing. He called it *standing at the edge of the question that changes everything.*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz admitted he literally had no idea why there was so much focus on him.
source_quote: I said what I actually believed, which is a thing I do less often than I probably should: 'I literally have no idea why there's all this focus on me.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir went very still when Asha Vandree declared herself in charge.
source_quote: The moment Asha Vandree declared herself in charge, something in me went very still.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought Asha's confidence was the problem because she had already decided she'd won.
source_quote: She said it with the absolute confidence of someone who had just survived something she shouldn't have — chaos, screaming, close calls that she'd already reframed as divine favor — and that confidence was the problem. *Excellent! Now that I am in charge!* ... Asha had already decided.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalled a saying from the Garden Shadow about the most dangerous person being the one who has already decided they've won.
source_quote: I've read rooms like this before. The Garden Shadow had a saying — or possibly Brother Quellin did, the one with the dusty robes who taught something about pressure points of social authority ... that the most dangerous person in a room isn't the one with the blade drawn. It's the one who has already decided they've won.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir remembered a class on decisive action under moral uncertainty taught by Brother Harren, though he didn't recall what was said.
source_quote: There was a class for this. Decisive action under moral uncertainty — the ethics of necessary violence, or something like that. I think it was Brother Harren, the one who never sat down, who taught it. I don't remember what he said. I remember it went on for a long time.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir made the decision to kill Asha Vandree because he believed someone had to make the call.
source_quote: I'm making a call," I said. ... I just happened to also be true. Someone had to make the call. I made it. That's all.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir did not look at Asha's body after killing her.
source_quote: I didn't look at the body.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin tried to retain the Drow sisters and asked what it would cost.
source_quote: Thorin, to his credit, tried to retain them. He asked what it would cost.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin refused to kill Asha Vandree without necessity, stating he didn't like killing people if he didn't have to.
source_quote: I don't like killing people if I don't have to," Thorin said. "I mean, you know...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was probably filing away a theological observation about mysterious dispensations.
source_quote: Grygum was probably filing away some theological observation about mysterious dispensations.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum looked thoughtful when Daz suggested auditing the books of the mysterious payer.
source_quote: No one laughed. Grygum looked thoughtful, which is his equivalent.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed that Thorin's reluctance, Nym and Kaelira's calculation, Grygum's preference for alternatives, and Daz's neutrality were all reasonable and true.
source_quote: All of it was reasonable. All of it was true. I just happened to also be true.
